title: When Validators Don’t Trigger: A Paired Evaluation of Generate→Validate→Repair for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (N=600 task pairs) to test whether a validator‑guided repair pipeline (generate→validate→repair) reduces high‑risk semantic misconfigurations relative to single‑shot LLM generation in intent→vendor‑configuration tasks. Under the preregistered adapter contract (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate) exactly one sampled initial candidate per pair was reused by both arms; the guarded arm could differ from baseline only if the deterministic validator rejected that candidate and an automated repair executed. Using gpt-5-mini as the generator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the validator, all 600 shared initial candidates passed the validator in both baseline and guarded conditions (baseline = 600/600; guarded = 600/600). The paired absolute difference = 0.0 (95% bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). No automated repairs were invoked. We report preregistration and execution-accounting details, clarify the scientific meaning of shared_initial_candidate semantics and the archived model sampling record (temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling), and discuss construct validity of validators, design implications for future NetOps safety evaluations, and limitations of this null but informative outcome.

sections.introduction: Intent‑driven NetOps aims to translate high‑level operator intents into correct low‑level, vendor‑specific device configurations. Prior work demonstrates prototype intent→configuration systems and proposes tool‑augmentation (validators, calculators, or deterministic checks) to reduce LLM errors, but open questions remain about operational reliability under adversarial or out‑of‑distribution intents and about rigorous workflow‑centered evaluation [1]–[3]. We preregistered a focused confirmatory study to answer: Under a paired design with shared_initial_candidate generation semantics, does a validator‑guided repair pipeline reduce high‑risk semantic failures relative to accepting a single LLM generation? Our contributions are (1) a preregistered paired experiment executed on 600 intent→configuration pairs with full archived artifacts; (2) a precise, artifact‑grounded interpretation of the observed null outcome under shared_initial_candidate semantics; and (3) practical recommendations for future generate→validate→repair evaluations.
sections.related_work: Work on LLM‑based intent translation and intent‑driven configuration generation has produced multiple prototype systems and testbed evaluations that show feasibility on constrained corpora [1], [2]. Surveys of agentic and safety‑oriented workflows report that tool‑augmentation (external validators, retrieval, calculators) can reduce classes of errors across domains, though reported gains are heterogeneous and often task‑dependent [3], [4]. Hallucination and semantic/functional errors in LLM‑generated code and configurations are well documented and motivate generate→validate→repair and constrained‑decoding approaches; constrained or neurosymbolic decoding can increase syntactic validity but requires domain grammars or tooling [5], [6]. Our study empirically examines one operational instantiation (deterministic validator + single permitted automated repair) under the strict shared_initial_candidate execution contract; consequently, the confirmatory estimand measures validator/repair trigger effectiveness rather than independent generation differences.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study was preregistered as autocand-2026-01-prereg-v1 before observing outcomes. The confirmatory paired design used 600 deterministically selected task pairs (planned_episode_count = 1200; complete_pair_count = 600). Primary estimand: the paired absolute difference in high‑risk semantic failure proportions (guarded − baseline), computed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 using an exact McNemar test and paired bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) per the preregistered analysis plan. Adapter, model, and generation semantics: the adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the declared generator was gpt-5-mini. Generation semantics were preregistered and executed as shared_initial_candidate: exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was produced and reused unchanged by both baseline and guarded conditions; only a validator‑triggered repair (at most one per guarded episode) could create a paired outcome difference. This execution contract was not changed post‑hoc. Model sampling record: the archived model configuration file is execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) and it records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. All runtime sampling fields and provider traces are archived for reproducibility. Tasks and validator: Tasks were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (synthetic intent→configuration items with explicit required sequences and workflow constraints). Deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule to produce a binary pass/fail and a detailed validator trace; the guarded arm permitted at most one automated repair call only when the validator failed. Inclusion/exclusion and contamination: confirmatory sample items required public provenance and license tags per the preregistered contamination plan. Analysis choices and power: preregistration assumed a baseline high‑risk failure rate ≈10% for power calibration (MDE = 5 percentage points, 80% power). The observed baseline rate was 0% (ceiling), so the preregistered power assumptions do not apply post‑hoc; we report exact paired results and discuss interpretive consequences in Discussion. Reproducibility pointers: execution manifest, raw_results.jsonl, model_configuration.json, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived at the manifest paths listed in the execution record.
sections.results: Execution accounting: The execution manifest records started_at_utc = 2026‑09‑01T10:38:58.473006+00:00, completed_at_utc = 2026‑09‑01T11:51:07.037898+00:00, planned_episode_count = 1200, completed_episode_count = 1200, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 600 (one shared initial generation per pair). Primary outcomes: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepted the shared initial candidate in every episode. Counts: baseline_success_count = 600/600 (100%), guarded_success_count = 600/600 (100%). Paired contingency: n11 = 600, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. No guarded repair calls executed because no validator failures occurred. Secondary preregistered estimands (vendor strata, repair success rate, failure‑mode breakdown) are uninformative because no failures occurred; archived analysis artifacts nevertheless include the empty/fully passed summaries (see analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Representative artifacts: several task‑level scoring examples and validator traces are archived (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000004-baseline.json), showing validator decisions and shared_initial_candidate reuse.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: Under the executed contract (shared_initial_candidate), the guarded pipeline can change a paired outcome only if the deterministic validator rejects the initial candidate and a repair produces a validator‑passing configuration. In this run the validator passed all initial candidates, so no repair opportunities occurred and the guarded pipeline produced no observable benefit. This null result is scientifically informative: it highlights that (a) the choice of generation semantics (shared initial draw versus independent per‑condition draws) determines what the paired estimand measures; (b) validator construct validity and sensitivity are central—an overpermissive validator can produce ceiling effects that mask differences; and (c) archival records of runtime sampling (temperature = null/unset in execution/model_configuration.json, SHA‑256 = a40e96e2...) must be interpreted carefully because null/unset does not establish deterministic sampling. Design implications and recommended practices: (1) When the scientific goal is to measure generation‑level differences, use independent per‑condition draws rather than shared_initial_candidate. (2) Audit validators (seeded or adversarial audits) to quantify sensitivity/specificity before confirmatory comparisons; if such audits are unavailable, report that validator sensitivity is an unresolved limitation. (3) Use adversarial or harder task banks to avoid ceiling effects. Limitations: synthetic task set and single‑model execution limit external generality; validator sensitivity was not independently audited in the archived confirmatory artifacts (see Limitations list). Consequences for H1/H2: the preregistered H1 (tool‑augmentation reduces high‑risk failures) and H2 (≥5 percentage‑point absolute reduction) could not be evaluated because the baseline rate was 0%, violating the power assumptions and removing the possibility of observing the preregistered minimal detectable effect; we therefore report the exact paired null outcome and recommend replication under designs that yield nonzero baseline failure rates.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=600 pairs) comparing single‑shot LLM generation and a validator‑guided repair pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Both conditions passed the deterministic validator in all pairs (100% baseline and guarded success), yielding an observed paired difference of 0.0 (95% CI [0.0, 0.0], p = 1.0). No repairs were invoked. This outcome stresses that (1) paired execution semantics critically determine what the experiment measures (validator/repair trigger effectiveness vs. generation differences), (2) validators must be audited for construct validity to avoid ceiling effects, and (3) measurement of generate→validate→repair benefits requires challenging task banks or independent generation arms. We archive all execution and analysis artifacts and provide concrete recommendations for future work testing generate→validate→repair pipelines.

disclosure_statement: Models, tools, and preregistration: Generative calls used the declared model gpt-5-mini via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. The deterministic validator was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. The study was preregistered as autocand-2026-01-prereg-v1 and executed under that preregistration. Autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family and approved the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the lock the AI system autonomously selected the final research question, executed the preregistered experiment, performed analyses, and drafted the manuscript. No manual human editing of technical content, numerical results, or manuscript conclusions occurred after the autonomy lock. Master prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Generation semantics and sampling: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per pair was reused by baseline and guarded); archived model configuration is execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820) and records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The Disclosure is intentionally concise; full execution manifests, raw model calls, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived at the manifest paths listed in the execution record.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded used the identical sampled initial generation per pair; thus guarded could create a difference only if the validator rejected that initial candidate and a repair executed. This design measures validator/repair trigger effectiveness, not independent generation differences.

Validator construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepted all initial candidates in this run; without an independent validator sensitivity audit this ceiling performance limits inference about the utility of tool augmentation across other task banks.

Task external validity: tasks were synthetic items from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with preregistered contamination/redaction rules; results may not generalize to diverse production configurations or vendor idiosyncrasies.
Model and adapter scope: only the declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one adapter instance were used; no claim of model‑class generality is made.

Sampling record: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is explicitly not evidence of deterministic sampling. Independent per‑condition sampling would be required to evaluate generation‑level effects.

Power assumptions violated: the preregistration's power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline failure rate (≈10%). The observed baseline rate was 0%, so the preregistered minimal detectable effect (5 percentage points) and power interpretation do not apply to this execution.
